content.body:
The QF.6pdr began development as early as 1938, when it was evident that armor levels would soon outstrip the ability of the QF.2pdr to penetrate. Built on a more conventional split-fork trail with a gunshield, the 6pdr proved to be an exceptionally hard-hitting gun capable of handling every tank in the German inventory until the introduction of the Tiger.
This gun is a terrific ambush gun, even at extreme ranges out to 1000m+. It fires a very flat shot, so first round hits are common. Note that it does NOT have any sort of range adjustment or range gradations, so offline practice is recommended until you get a good feel for how the shots drop at longer ranges. Against German tanks, aim at anything besides the mantlet (the front of the turret) for an almost-certain penetration.
Heavily armoured AFV's like the StuGs and the Tiger should not be engaged from the frontal aspect ... instead relocate and seek a better angle or a different victim, although a quick shot to the track should immobilize it and may offer you the opportunity to get away unscathed.
